title: A Bad Reign and a Hidden Prince
overview: Judah's young king Ahaziah follows his mother's family into ruin and is killed, then his mother Athaliah wipes out the royal family and takes the throne, while one baby prince is secretly saved.

parts.label: The youngest son crowned (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Raiders had killed Ahaziah's older brothers, so the people of Jerusalem made the youngest son king, and he reigned only one year. The standard Hebrew text here gives his age as forty two, which cannot fit since his father died at forty, so most scholars follow 2 Kings and some ancient translations in reading twenty two and see forty two as an early copying error.

parts.label: Led by his mother's family (vv. 3-6)
parts.note: His mother Athaliah came from the family of Omri and Ahab, the rulers of the northern kingdom of Israel who promoted worship of the god Baal, and after his father died her relatives became his advisers. They drew him into a war beside Joram, Israel's king, against Hazael of Aram (roughly modern Syria), and Joram went home to Jezreel wounded.

parts.label: Caught in Jehu's purge (vv. 7-9)
parts.note: The writer says God used Ahaziah's visit to Joram to bring him down, because Jehu, an army commander chosen by God to destroy Ahab's family, struck while Ahaziah was there and killed Judah's officials and Ahaziah's young relatives. Ahaziah was hunted down and killed, though he was given a proper burial out of respect for his faithful grandfather Jehoshaphat.

parts.label: Athaliah seizes power (v. 10)
parts.note: With her son dead, Athaliah had the rest of Judah's royal family killed and ruled in their place. The text does not give her motive, though the killings plainly cleared her way to the throne.

parts.label: One child hidden (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: Ahaziah's sister Jehosheba, wife of the priest Jehoiada, rescued baby Joash from the slaughter and hid him in the temple buildings for six years while Athaliah ruled. This kept King David's family line from dying out, and Christians later read it as protecting the line that would lead to Jesus.
